title: Jabali tries to persuade Rama to accept the Kingdom
introduction: A Brahmana named Jabali tries to persuade Rama to accept the kingdom by advocating the theory of Nastikas (non-believers), saying that he need not get attached to his father's words and remain in the troublesome forest. Jabali requests Rama to enjoy the royal luxuries, by accepting the crown.
closing: इत्यार्षे श्रीमद्रामायणे आदिकाव्ये अयोध्याकाण्डे अष्टोत्तरशततमः सर्गः
Thus completes 108th Chapter of Ayodhya Kanda of the glorious Ramayana of Valmiki, the work of a sage and the oldest epic.

verses.devanagari:
आश्वासयन्तम् भरतम् जाबालिर् ब्राह्मण उत्तमः |
उवाच रामम् धर्मज्नम् धर्म अपेतम् इदम् वचः
verses.iast:
āśvāsayantam bharatam jābālir brāhmaṇa uttamaḥ |
uvāca rāmam dharmajnam dharma apetam idam vacaḥ
verses.translation: A brahmana called Jabali spoke the following unrighteous words to Rama, who knew righteousness and who was assuaging Bharata as aforesaid

verses.devanagari:
साधु राघव मा भूत् ते बुद्धिर् एवम् निरर्थका |
प्राकृतस्य नरस्य इव आर्य बुद्धेः तपस्विनः
verses.iast:
sādhu rāghava mā bhūt te buddhir evam nirarthakā |
prākṛtasya narasya iva ārya buddheḥ tapasvinaḥ
verses.translation: "Enough, O Rama! Let not your wisdom be rendered void like a common man, you who are distinguished for your intelligence and virtue."

glosses.meaning: who are distinguished for your intelligence

verses.devanagari:
कः कस्य पुरुषो बन्धुः किम् आप्यम् कस्य केनचित् |
यद् एको जायते जन्तुर् एक एव विनश्यति
verses.iast:
kaḥ kasya puruṣo bandhuḥ kim āpyam kasya kenacit |
yad eko jāyate jantur eka eva vinaśyati
verses.translation: "Who is related to whom? What is there to be obtained by anything and by whom? Every creature is born alone and dies alone."

verses.devanagari:
तस्मान् माता पिता च इति राम सज्जेत यो नरः |
उन्मत्त इव स ज्नेयो न अस्ति काचिद्द् हि कस्यचित्
verses.iast:
tasmān mātā pitā ca iti rāma sajjeta yo naraḥ |
unmatta iva sa jneyo na asti kācidd hi kasyacit
verses.translation: "O, Rama! He who clings to another, saying, 'This is my father, this is my mother, he should be known as one who has lost his wits. There is none who belongs to another."

glosses.meaning: as one who has lost his wits

verses.devanagari:
यथा ग्राम अन्तरम् गग्च्छन् नरः कश्चिद् क्वचिद् वसेत् |
उत्सृज्य च तम् आवासम् प्रतिष्ठेत अपरे अहनि
एवम् एव मनुष्याणाम् पिता माता गृहम् वसु |
आवास मात्रम् काकुत्स्थ सज्जन्ते न अत्र सज्जनाः
verses.iast:
yathā grāma antaram gagcchan naraḥ kaścid kvacid vaset |
utsṛjya ca tam āvāsam pratiṣṭheta apare ahani
evam eva manuṣyāṇām pitā mātā gṛham vasu |
āvāsa mātram kākutstha sajjante na atra sajjanāḥ
verses.translation: "O, Rama! As one who passes the a strange village spends the night the and the next day leaves that place and continues his journey, so are mother, father, home and possessions to a man; they are but a resting place. The wise do not become attached to them".

glosses.meaning: they are but a resting place

verses.devanagari:
पित्र्यम् राज्यम् समुत्सृज्य स न अर्हति नर उत्तम |
आस्थातुम् कापथम् दुह्खम् विषमम् बहु कण्टकम्
verses.iast:
pitryam rājyam samutsṛjya sa na arhati nara uttama |
āsthātum kāpatham duhkham viṣamam bahu kaṇṭakam
verses.translation: "O, chief of men! You as such should not abandon your father's kingdom in order to dwell in a lonely forest, that is excruciating hard to traverse and full of thorny thickets."

verses.devanagari:
समृद्धायाम् अयोध्यायाम् आत्मानम् अभिषेचय |
एक वेणी धरा हि त्वाम् नगरी सम्प्रतीक्षते
verses.iast:
samṛddhāyām ayodhyāyām ātmānam abhiṣecaya |
eka veṇī dharā hi tvām nagarī sampratīkṣate
verses.translation: "Get yourself crowned in the prosperous kingdom of Ayodhya. That city is waiting for you, with your locks duly unfound."

verses.devanagari:
राज भोगान् अनुभवन् महा अर्हान् पार्थिव आत्मज |
विहर त्वम् अयोध्यायाम् यथा शक्रः त्रिविष्टपे
verses.iast:
rāja bhogān anubhavan mahā arhān pārthiva ātmaja |
vihara tvam ayodhyāyām yathā śakraḥ triviṣṭape
verses.translation: "O, prince! Enjoy the royal luxuries worthy of you. Move around in Ayodhya as Indra the Lord of celestials does in heaven!"

glosses.meaning: as Indra the Lord of Celestials

verses.devanagari:
न ते कश्चिद् दशरतहः त्वम् च तस्य न कश्चन |
अन्यो राजा त्वम् अन्यः च तस्मात् कुरु यद् उच्यते
verses.iast:
na te kaścid daśaratahḥ tvam ca tasya na kaścana |
anyo rājā tvam anyaḥ ca tasmāt kuru yad ucyate
verses.translation: "Dasaratha is none to you nor you in anyway to him. That king is another and your are another. Hence, do what is told by me?"

verses.devanagari:
बीजमात्रम् पिता जन्तोः शुक्लं रुधिरमेव च |
संयुक्तमृतुमन्मात्रा पुरुषस्येह जन्म तत्
verses.iast:
bījamātram pitā jantoḥ śuklaṃ rudhirameva ca |
saṃyuktamṛtumanmātrā puruṣasyeha janma tat
verses.translation: "The father is only the seed of a being. The sperm and the ovum blend at the right time in the mother's womb, so that a human being is born in this world."

verses.devanagari:
गतः स नृपतिः तत्र गन्तव्यम् यत्र तेन वै |
प्रवृत्तिर् एषा मर्त्यानाम् त्वम् तु मिथ्या विहन्यसे
verses.iast:
gataḥ sa nṛpatiḥ tatra gantavyam yatra tena vai |
pravṛttir eṣā martyānām tvam tu mithyā vihanyase
verses.translation: "The king has gone, where he had to go. This is the fate of all being unnecessarily, you are still frustrated over the matter."

verses.devanagari:
अर्थ धर्म परा ये ये तामः तान् शोचामि न इतरान् |
ते हि दुह्खम् इह प्राप्य विनाशम् प्रेत्य भेजिरे
verses.iast:
artha dharma parā ye ye tāmḥ tān śocāmi na itarān |
te hi duhkham iha prāpya vināśam pretya bhejire
verses.translation: "I pity all those whosoever, devoted to wealth and religious merit, not other (who are devoted to sense-enjoyment), for, they, having undergone suffering in this life, have met with extermination after death."

glosses.meaning: devoted to wealth and religious merit

verses.devanagari:
अष्टका पितृ दैवत्यम् इत्य् अयम् प्रसृतो जनः |
अन्नस्य उपद्रवम् पश्य मृतो हि किम् अशिष्यति
verses.iast:
aṣṭakā pitṛ daivatyam ity ayam prasṛto janaḥ |
annasya upadravam paśya mṛto hi kim aśiṣyati
verses.translation: "These people say, 'The eighth day should be given up to sacrifices for the spirits of our ancestors.' See the waste of food. What will a dead man eat?"

glosses.meaning: should be given up to sacrifices for the spirits of our ancestors

verses.devanagari:
यदि भुक्तम् इह अन्येन देहम् अन्यस्य गग्च्छति |
दद्यात् प्रवसतः श्राद्धम् न तत् पथ्य् अशनम् भवेत्
verses.iast:
yadi bhuktam iha anyena deham anyasya gagcchati |
dadyāt pravasataḥ śrāddham na tat pathy aśanam bhavet
verses.translation: "If food eaten by one here, reaches another's body, then let a sacrifice be offered for those who are setting out on a distant journey. Will it not become a food on their path?"

glosses.meaning: for those who are setting out on a distant journey

verses.devanagari:
दान सम्वनना ह्य् एते ग्रन्था मेधाविभिः कृताः |
यजस्व देहि दीक्षस्व तपः तप्यस्व सम्त्यज
verses.iast:
dāna samvananā hy ete granthā medhāvibhiḥ kṛtāḥ |
yajasva dehi dīkṣasva tapaḥ tapyasva samtyaja
verses.translation: "Perform sacrifices, distribute gifts, consecrate yourselves, practise ansterity and renunciation' - These writings are composed by learned men for the sake of inducing others to give."

glosses.meaning: for the sake of inducing others to give.

verses.devanagari:
स न अस्ति परम् इत्य् एव कुरु बुद्धिम् महा मते |
प्रत्यक्षम् यत् तद् आतिष्ठ परोक्षम् पृष्ठतः कुरु
verses.iast:
sa na asti param ity eva kuru buddhim mahā mate |
pratyakṣam yat tad ātiṣṭha parokṣam pṛṣṭhataḥ kuru
verses.translation: "O, the highly wise! Arrive at a conclusion, therefore, that there is nothing beyond this Universe. Give precedence to that which meets the eye and turn your back on what is beyond our knowledge."

glosses.meaning: on what is beyond our knowledge.

verses.devanagari:
सताम् बुद्धिम् पुरः कृत्य सर्व लोक निदर्शिनीम् |
राज्यम् त्वम् प्रतिगृह्णीष्व भरतेन प्रसादितः
verses.iast:
satām buddhim puraḥ kṛtya sarva loka nidarśinīm |
rājyam tvam pratigṛhṇīṣva bharatena prasāditaḥ
verses.translation: "Honour the judgment of the wise and regarding that which is approved by all, accept the kingdom as propitiated by Bharata."

glosses.meaning: and regarding that which is approved by all
